diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Kubernetes add-ons module is launched without the configured data-plane wait value, so it can install add-ons before the managed node group is ready. Wire the node-group ARN into data_plane_wait_arn to make the existing dataplane wait gate it.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The root Kubernetes-addons module is not gated on the managed node group becoming available. This example provisions add-ons that expect a usable EKS data plane, and its data_plane_wait_arn input is left at its empty default rather than being wired to the node-group output. Make the module wait for the managed node group before deploying add-ons.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The stateful example enables EKS managed node groups but does not pass their ARN through data_plane_wait_arn or otherwise order Kubernetes add-on deployment after the managed node group. Add-ons may begin before worker nodes are available, affecting workload scheduling and data-plane-dependent add-ons.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
The `gp3` StorageClass uses the `ebs.csi.aws.com` provisioner, which is only registered once the EBS CSI driver add-on is installed. That driver is provisioned by `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_self_managed_aws_ebs_csi_driver = true`), but `kubernetes_storage_class_v1.gp3` has no attribute reference or `depends_on` expressing that ordering, so it can be created before the driver exists. It should depend on the add-ons module that installs the EBS CSI driver.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The `gp3` StorageClass uses provisioner `ebs.csi.aws.com`, which is registered by the AWS EBS CSI driver installed via `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_self_managed_aws_ebs_csi_driver = true`). It has no expressed dependency on that module, so Terraform may create the StorageClass before the provisioner exists. It should depend on `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`:resource.kubernetes_storage_class_v1.gp3` uses the provisioner `ebs.csi.aws.com`, which is provided by the self-managed aws-ebs-csi-driver Helm add-on installed by `:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons`. The graph shows no dependency (implicit or explicit) on that module, so Terraform may create the gp3 storage class before the EBS CSI driver is deployed (or destroy the driver first), leaving PVCs backed by this class unusable.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.kubernetes_storage_class_v1.gp3` uses the `ebs.csi.aws.com` provisioner, which is provided by the aws-ebs-csi-driver add-on installed via `:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (enable_self_managed_aws_ebs_csi_driver = true). There is no attribute reference or depends_on linking the storage class to that module, so the storage class can be created before the CSI driver's Helm release is deployed and volumes provisioned against this class can fail.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
The `efs` StorageClass uses the `efs.csi.aws.com` provisioner, which is only registered once the EFS CSI driver add-on is installed. That driver is provisioned by `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true`). `kubernetes_storage_class_v1.efs` correctly depends on `module.efs` (via `fileSystemId = module.efs.id`) but has no dependency on the driver that actually implements `efs.csi.aws.com`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The `efs` StorageClass uses provisioner `efs.csi.aws.com`, which is registered by the AWS EFS CSI driver installed via `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true`). While it references `module.efs.id`, it has no dependency on the CSI driver addon, so it may be created before the provisioner is available. It should also depend on `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`:resource.kubernetes_storage_class_v1.efs` references `module.efs.id` (captured in its implicit deps) and uses the provisioner `efs.csi.aws.com`, which is provided by the aws-efs-csi-driver add-on installed by `:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true`). There is no dependency on that module, so the storage class can be created while the EFS CSI driver is not yet installed, making dynamically provisioned EFS volumes fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.kubernetes_storage_class_v1.efs` uses the `efs.csi.aws.com` provisioner (dynamic provisioning via `provisioningMode = efs-ap`), which is provided by the aws-efs-csi-driver add-on installed via `:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true). It only depends on `:module.efs` (for `fileSystemId`), not on the addons module, so the storage class can be created before the EFS CSI driver is running and PVCs against it cannot be provisioned.
